reviews.review_description: Extremely disappointing and unreliable service.**The attached photo shows how my roof was left completely damaged after their solar panel installation. Even worse, for over two weeks, they’ve ignored my requests for a proper resolution. Their attitude was unprofessional—they even refused to connect the service unless the full payment was made, despite the poor workmanship.I deeply regret choosing this company. Save yourself the trouble and go with a more affordable, respectful competitor. As of now, the issue remains unresolved.

- Prompt, 6.6 KW system.I can't say if it's reducing my Elect' bills as the feed-in part of the whole process still hasn't been set-up (1 month after installation)- Installers were fantastic, couldn't fault their work ethic, attention to detail and communication throughout the install process. Maybe could've cleaned up a bit better but nothing 5mins with an air blower didn't fix.- After agreeing to an installation date, 6 weeks in advance, was emailed from Primero the week before the agreed installation date that it couldn't be done due to no availability of installers and it needs to be rescheduled (just so happens it was a long weekend, Friday P/H).I stood my ground and told Primero to honor their agreed installation date.2hrs later I received comm's that my installation will be going ahead on the originally agreed date.The installer ran quickly through the Invertor, Isolation point in meter box and what he was seeing on the App on his mobile phone. Then he said that the office will contact you to run through in more detail how to use the system.I ended up contacting Primero to get this information, after waiting for a week.Solar P.V system has been installed for over a month now and I'm still not seeing any feed into the grid. I've contacted my Elect' area wholesaler/ Retailer to follow up.After sales/ Installation contact is non-existent with Primero, which is worrying if anything goes wrong.

Sales and design process was easy and very quick to communicate. System design accommodated 6.6kw of panels on a 2 story townhouse roof, combination of panels mounted portrait and landscape orientation across 3 different roof faces/directions (north east and west).Installers turned up on time as per the booking date, which was one of my suggested booking dates to accommodate my time off work. 3 very professional workers, 1 sparky and 2 roofers/installers were able to complete the installation in 1 full day. I do have reason to believe that at least the sparky (not sure about the other 2) were sub contractors, they were all still great however the Primero website does boast about having their own team, so just nit-picking here.About 2 weeks after install the inspector turned up, this passed and the system was switched on - still waiting DNSP paperwork/process to enable full 5kw feed in. There was a paperwork issue with our address being listed incorrectly which has delayed this slightly. Follow-up requests about this to Primero has been a little slow to respond, took a 2nd email to get a response from them. So some of their aftersales service is not as prompt as the sales process was.2 things about Primero that do concern me: 1: their email is not complaint with SPF/DMARC polices which (aside from the spoofing/security concerns) often leads to their emails landing in the junk folder. 2: not long after my install their website went down for about 2 weeks, leading me to being concerned they may have gone out of business right after my install - however the site is now back up and they were responding to emails.All in all Primero did well for us and I don't regret choosing them. The design, price, prompt install date and install process/quality was all top notch. Aftersales enquires could be a little more prompt and I hope they soon get SPF/DMARC figured out for their emails.
Fantastic advice and service from everyone at Primero. We heartily endorse and recommend them

Ashley, Andre and the installation team lead by Dylan did their jobs expertly and listened and responded patiently and professionally to my many questions as I learned what was involved with a large solar and battery installation.Most importantly they delivered a result to my exact requirements.

Company was great to deal with. Least pushy of all the ones I spoke to, but best price and detailed quotes. Did research before our conversation about our address using maps which impressed me. Everyone was great.
Make sure they inspect the site before the install. Too many changes made on the day.

-Sales and Support were super-responsive over email and phone-System seems to be working well a month after installation (eg. sustained periods at the 10kW inverter limit)-They told me they've been using the same sub-contractors for installation for many years. They were professional and very quick.Very minor negatives:-There was a small amount of rubbish left on site eg. a couple of bolts and mounting brackets dropped from the roof on the ground at the side of the house, a couple of scraps of electrical tape left in the roof gutters, a few tile clips displaced, and they left one of the adhesive safety signs lying in the gutter- I stuck it on the solar array later. The holes they drilled into the brickwork for the inverter cables were too big, I filled the gaps afterwards. Mounting frames were too long, extending well beyond where the array was. There was an attempt to cut the end off one frame, but it looks like they gave up before they cut all the way through. They drilled the electrical safety sign into our man hole ceiling cover, but the screws were too long so they now protrude through the cover. The lead electrician was very business-like, maybe a touch unfriendly as I felt he just wanted to get the job done and move on.-Follow-up was where they slipped a bit, but this may have been because it was over Dec/Jan holiday period-> It wasn't made clear to me what needed to be done after the physical installation.-> Electrical inspection is officially supposed to happen within 8 days of installation, but this didn't happen till I did my own research to discover this, after which I had to chase them up.-> Meter needed to be configured for Grid Feed-In. It took a while for them to start this process.-> Solar generation was initially only below 1kW. After a firmware update of the inverter, it started to work, but I had tofigure out for myself how to do this.

Overall, I was very happy with the service and installation quality.The sales & quoting process was smooth and informative. The sales rep was not in any way pushy, and was willing to take the time to answer all my questions.  It was also obvious that he knew what he was talking about and was quite experienced in the field.The installation was professional and the technicians were friendly and helpful.  They helped set up the mobile app afterwards and demonstrated how to use it.There were a couple of areas which I think could have been improved on:1. The installation was booked for first thing in the morning on the agreed date, however the installers did not arrive until early afternoon due to working on another home.  This caused the completion to be delayed to another day as they ran out of time.  Whilst this was not overly inconvenient, it did mean that I had to re-arrange my schedule to accommodate the second day.2. The company advertises itself on the basis that it employs their own electricians to perform the work and presents this as a competitive advantage.  Our installation was, however, performed by a subcontractor.  Whilst there is nothing to suggest that the work was not performed to a high standard, and the subcontractor was friendly and helpful, I think it is misleading to advertise your organisation in a certain way if that is not the reality.

Everyone at Primero Electric & Solar have been absolutely FANTASTIC and made my solar system installation an absolute breeze!From Ash who endured many an email & phone call to answer all my queries & roof design tweaks (because I'm one of THOSE kinds of customers) to Andre & Ciara in the office who set up the installation within the limited days I had available & of course Darcy & his team of installers, each and every one had my solar system installed within a month of my initial enquiries...I can VERY HIGHLY recommend Primero Electric & Solar!FYI - The 4x panels that are in the shade in the pic are facing west to maximise the solar gain in winter once the tree has lost its leaves

Prompt communication, understood and catered to our needs. Very fast at organising installation and followed through with paper work very efficiently. Still answered our calls and enquiries promptly even after installation and payment. Very happy with Primero Solar.

Primero did a fantastic job from start to end. Well communicated and everything was done according to the plan. Thanks for all staff members for their professional work.
Primero Solar where fantastic from the quoting stage to the install and connectionAlway keeping me informedTook around 5 weeks to be installed and 4 days after for inspection and turn onPerfect

Installing Solar is not for the faint hearted - all the steps need to be followed to get to a successful outcome.   SQ made the process easier by getting us three quotes, however it still was like comparing apples, oranges and bananas!    Do your research!  We found that that things were changing so quickly we had to make sure the reviews we were reading related to the particular panels and inverters that were on offer and not a previous or later version.The crew at Primero were happy to answer all our question even when we went back with multiple queries.  On the day of installation the team were amazing - courteous, professional and as we now know from the inspector they did a wonderful job. Also two of our neighbours who saw the installation team (and are currently looking to install solar) asked for details of the company involved as they could see the efficient and professional way that they went about their job.Also it may be obvious but  when everything has settled down and all is working, do a check of electricity prices on the the compare sites - the way electricity is charged changes when you install solar and depending on your lifestyle and usage it may be wise to change retailers - again do your research.Thank you to all involved. May the sun keeping shining and may the rain fall at night.

Primero is a professional organisation and was an absolute joy to deal with. To me the whole solar process dealing with Primero was easy and stress free.It started with Ash providing the quotes in a timely manner and then answering all my questions. Once I made my decision to proceed with Primero, I was contacted the next day and an installation date booked in.  The installers led by Dillon where punctual, polite, professional and extremely tidy and did a wonderful job. I was also shown which solar app to download and provided with login details.From there, the rest of the team, in Customer Support, Client Support & Office Administrator made the whole process of connecting to the grid easy and it was done in a timely manner. The team did all the work, in providing my energy company all the required certificates to enable me to connect to the grid.The solar app, I must admit becomes a bit addictive, but I'm sure that will settle down over time!Overall, I'm extremely happy with the entire solar service provided by Primero. It was done in a professional and timely manner and would like to thank everybody in the entire team for making it an easy and stress-free experience for me.
Installation was completed timely and to a very good level. Arrived on time and got straight to work, also cleaned up after themselves as well as replaced broken tiles.

Very happy with everything from quoting to after sales service. It was a big job - taking 4 men a whole day.Quoting was a smooth process. Sales / design staff were quite keen to follow up on their leads from Solar Quotes. Out of all the three quotes, it really felt like Primero were the most understanding of my requirements and the trade-offs between cost, performance and reliability. Very flexible in their approach and answered all my questions. They listen to your needs and avoid falling into the trap of giving you 'throwaway lines' like "Fronius is the best" or "You must use a fully optimised system."No obligation site survey included to appease any remaining concerns about fitment.On the day of installation the team was punctual and efficient. Power was only off for a short amount of time which was impressive given the amount of switchboard reconfiguration required.Big enough company to have the economics of scale to offer great value of money yet appears to work as tight knit team who really comes across as caring about every customer. For example, when I had to call their office to ask a question - the usual person helping with my installation was not available yet the team member who answered the phone still seemed to have first hand knowledge about my installation, when it was happening and all relevant information at their fingertips.Trickier questions that office staff could not answer on the spot were also not a problem. The office staff promised to get the lead electrician who installed the system to call me back with an answer and sure enough the next day he did.
Installer on time and helpful service so the way. Highly recommend.
Primers provided excellent support with researching requirements, organising rebates a day well coordinated installation
Everything went really smoothly, staff were polite and very helpful. They chased up grid connection and helped me ensure it was all done.

Quotes were quick and well detailed with item costs - and they kept providing adjusted quotes as I asked for changes to products in order to stay within my budget.Installation was prompt, punctual, polite and tidy. Very professional, trouble free installation and good communication throughout the process. Some delay , over 2 weeks for safety inspection. All going well, that is happening today.Unable to comment on grid connection or how it works as yet but I don't expect any problems. Very happy with the company.

I feel he was pulling the wool over my eyes & wanted to move to the next job.I did ring Primero customer service as I was upset & later spoke to a solar electricianMy electrician later came after inspection & installed a RCD ILO a circuit breaker it didn't need a separate power switch!

I received quotes from the3 companies you recommended: Green Edge, O'Brien and Primero. I also had discussions with Natural Solar, a NSW company who got in contact 'out of the blue'. All three recommended companies were professional, helpful and not at all 'pushy'. The 'solar designer' from Green Edge actually came out to view the property. We chose Primero as their price was the lowest.The installation was carried out within a couple of weeks by a group which were sub-contractors for Primero. They did the job in a day, which included removing existing panels and two large, very heavy glass panels which were backups for the gas water heating system (we had these panels disconnected, but they removed the panels from the roof) and installing 28 new panels plus the invertor and battery. The people who did it were tidy, punctual and polite. The head of the installation team showed us how everything worked, organised the grid connections and all we had to do was wait a couple of weeks for the inspection by the State government electrical inspector. He made a point to tell me how well the job was done. I was also relieved that the panels removed from our house (15 years old) were destined for Vietnam for use. We use iSolarCloud app on our phones to track how much electricity the panels are generating, the state of our battery and how much charge is going into the grid and how much we are using from the grid.

QuotingPrimero were quick to quote and have a good phone conversation.  They weren't the cheapest, but offered good choices and were happy to amend their quote multiple times to an East/West tilt design for the garage roof.  All other installers wanted to install flat on the garage, despite the negative 2 deg south roof.They were hesitant to undertake a site inspection, but with some nudging, one of their sub-contracted installers came out.  In doing so, (despite two other companies quoting on-site) they spotted a cable size issue to the garage sub-board, that would require a new trench between the detached garage/house.Unfortunately the necessary trench work also made the job complex and Primero initially refused to quote/proceed further.  A direct quote from the sub-contractor to keep feed to/from the garage separate from the solar install, brought Primero back into contention, and they stayed in the picture while also adding a battery to the quote.SystemSungrow 6kw hybrid inverterSungrow 9.6kwh battery (3 modules)Jinko Solar Tiger Neo 440w panels x 16Pre-installOnce Primero was awarded the job and a deposit paid in September, install was scheduled for mid-December.  Then began the long SolarVic process (mainly due to battery loan) that Primero didn't really help with.  With the approvals only coming 2 days prior to the scheduled install, I was told I'd lose my 2023 install date, as opposed to offered support with SolarVic.InstallationDillon from Dillzap Electrical completed the install with care and patience.  It was a full day install as commissioning the battery took hours, with network cabling issues.  I was explained how to turn the system on/off and guided through downloading the app, before the system was turned off until inspected.Post-installDespite being pre-Xmas, the system was loosely inspected 2 days later and has been running great since.  Maybe a little lower real-world power output than I was expecting, but have been 94% self-sufficient since inspection power-on.OverallWhile I'd recommend Primero, I'm really conscious that the sub-contractor did the hard yards, with the site inspection; trenching quote/work; solar install.  I'd probably contact them directly in the future.

Primero was very proactive and helpful with providing quick and timely quotes which was great. After getting quotes from a few companies we went with Primero and signed a contract based on the fact they they were the cheapest and seemed to be professional. We paid the deposit and then was set up for an install date in December.On the installation day, Primero's subcontractor turned up on site (who had not inspected previously) and decided that our roof was not suitable due to having old terracotta tiles and they did not want to therefore proceed with the installation due to the higher risk of damage to the old terracotta tiled roof.Very frustrating because nothing had changed since the job was quoted, deposit paid and contract signed.A waste of time, money & effort for all parties involved (myself loosing ~$600 of STCs this year and a day off work, Subcontractor and Primero).Primero explained that it is too costly for them to inspect when quoting because if they are not awarded the job, they cannot recoup the costs of inspecting. Although it's Primero's risk to manage (quoting and subcontracting without checking site conditions), the cost of the risk ultimately coming to fruition is shared with the customer if they decide to exit the contract.Overall, I'd highly recommend to others who might have an older house or a tiled roof to only consider engaging a solar installer who has actually inspected the site (which is common) and is aware of the site conditions when quoting rather than quoting from a desktop review only.

Quote Process:We ended up with five quotes from two suppliers across a range of prices, after discussing some options. Paul from Primero was excellent to deal with, taking the time to explain the various products being offered, the details of the quote, and assumptions like system efficiency. We get a bit of shade on parts of our roof and some times of the year, and we were keen to see how to get the most efficient system that would generate best from panels that have sun on them. Paul convinced us to go with the SolarEdge inverter which also comes with live monitoring via an app, which we were keen on, as we're also quite heavy power consumers and figured it would be great to see where we can make savings. We were shopping for solar for the second time. The first time, a few years ago, we didn't know about Solar Quotes and we went out to random suppliers, and ended up so confused we didn't buy anything. This time around we had the background info from Solar Quotes and Paul took us through the details.Installation:It went perfectly. Soon after we paid a deposit, we got an installation date locked in which was around four weeks hence. The guys turned up on time, were polite and great to deal with, taking the time to discuss and explain what was to be done, when they needed to turn the power off (we were working at home), showed us the system and the monitoring app (but we couldn't monitor it yet). They did a neat job and cleaned up after themselves, and were done by around mid afternoon. Couldn't hope for better.Follow-Up:We got our inspection by Energy Safe Victoria around two weeks later (that's out of Primero's control) - people looking for solar should know that the system stays turned off until it's inspected, and we're not complaining about the timing. There was one additional cost of $170 - the installers advised that an awning over the inverter was recommended to shade it from the sun. He recommended it to make sure it had the best chance of passing inspection. People shopping for solar should consider if the inverter is going to go on a north facing wall, you might need to get this added to the quote. I'm not bothered by the extra cost if it was needed to ensure a compliant system.Then we were asked to pay the balance of the cost, and Primero booked our inspection and arranged the grid connection (meter reconfiguration) with our electricity retailer. All went well.  People considering Primero should know that they'll ask for the balance of payment immediately after installation, and then they'll book the inspection. I understand some installers will ask for payment after the inspection. Prospective customers might want to consider if this is agreeable terms and conditions for them. I guess the only concern would be if it didn't pass inspection, you've already paid, and you need to get the installer to come back - but based on the reviews I read, a Primero installation was going to be good enough to pass inspection. I was a bit annoyed to get an auto-generated reminder at 6:20am the day after I paid. I would have hoped someone would check for overnight bank transfers before these are sent. But it's minor in the grand scheme of things.We had to ask a couple of times for our login details for the inverter to get set up on the app - only a minor gripe in the scheme of things, I get that they're busy. Then we were up and running with solar, around 6 weeks after paying the deposit, which we thought was great.Then we had an inverter fault after a week. Andre from Primero straight away contacted SolarEdge, who remotely connected to the inverter and updated the software. All sorted in a couple of hours which was great service.System Performance and Value:After a few weeks, it has been generating power at or above what Paul predicted in the quote for this time of the year, except for rainy days when you wouldn't expect it.  The monitoring is fantastic and we can already see how we can modify our usage to get the best value out of the system. It tells us that we're sending a lot of power back to the retailer who is paying us a pittance for it, and already making us think about when we'll install a battery.How do you rate value for money, when we had five quotes and opted for the most expensive? We're getting much more out of the monitoring than we ever could out of a basic system. The SolarEdge Home Hub inverter gives us the monitoring and options to go independent of the grid in the future. I always said that in a few years time I won't care that we paid a bit extra. So I rate it 5 out of 5.And all up, minor things aside, I'd definitely recommend Primero.
